content.what_it_is: MATLAB postprocessing script for the Mase-Kirby (1992) benchmark ('Make-Kirby' in header L1; 'Example 4.1' L4): compares skewness and asymmetry of computed surface elevation against experimental data and Kirby et al. reference results. Loads experimental mkskew_man.out (L9; row 1 skewness ske, row 2 asymmetry ae, L11-12), then 12 FUNWAVE station files sta_0001..sta_0012 (loop L22-26, names built via sprintf('%.2d',k) L23), converting eta to cm (*100, L25). Discards the first 399 samples ('remove the first 20 second data' L32; en=en(400:...) L34). Gauge depths h=[47 35 30 25 20 17.5 15 12.5 10 7.5 5 2.5] cm (L38). Statistics: demeaned enn (L41), stn=std (L44), skewness skn=sum(enn.^3)/nn./stn.^3 (L45); asymmetry via Hilbert transform hn=imag(hilbert(enn)) (L48), demeaned (L49), an=-sum(hnn.^3)/nn./std(hn).^3 (L52). Saves skew_asy.mat with h,ske,skn,ae,an (L54). Loads Kirby reference mkskew_kirby.out (L57; mskew L58, masy L60; self-assignments L59, L61 are no-ops). Plots all six curves vs depth with black o/x markers (L65-69), axis [0 50 -0.25 1.2] (L70), labels (L71-72), 6-entry legend (L74). Computes percentage RMSE of present model and Kirby model against data for skewness and asymmetry over gauges 2-12 (L77-81, unterminated by semicolons so values echo). Commented remnants: fread of etats.out (L15-17), alternate fdir path (L19), print skmk.ps (L84).
entities: script variables: mkskew @L9, ske @L11, ae @L12, fdir @L20, k @L22, num @L23, gage @L24, en @L25 (resized @L34), nn @L36 (record length; redefined as index range 2:12 @L64), h,nh,nhn @L38, enn @L41, stn @L44, skn @L45, hn @L48, hnn @L49, an @L52, manu @L57, mskew @L58, masy @L60, n @L63, sk_rmse_tvd @L77, sk_rmse_kirby @L78, as_rmse_tvd @L80, as_rmse_kirby @L81

equations.ref: percent RMSE vs data (also L78, L80, L81)

calls: clear all @L6; load @L9, @L24, @L57; sprintf @L23; length @L34, @L36; ones/mean @L41, @L49; std @L44, @L52; hilbert @L48; save @L54; plot @L65-69; axis/grid @L70; xlabel @L71; ylabel @L72; legend @L74; rmse @L77, @L78, @L80, @L81

verbatim_spans.text: save skew_asy.mat h ske skn ae an

unresolved: Variable nn is first the record length used in the skewness/asymmetry normalizations (L36, L45, L52) and is then silently redefined as the gauge index range 2:12 (L64) used in plotting and RMSE -- two unrelated meanings in one script.
L34 comment says remove the first 20 seconds but drops 399 samples; with the wavemaker script's dt=0.05 s that is ~20 s, yet the sampling interval of these station files is not stated here.
rmse() (L77-81) is not defined in this file and is not a classic built-in; requires an external function on the path.
mskew=mskew; and masy=masy; (L59, L61) are no-op self-assignments; bare string expressions at L14 and L29 serve only as progress echoes.
Header calls the experiment 'Make-Kirby (1992)' (L1) -- presumably Mase-Kirby per the directory name car_mase_kirby.
Gauge 1 (h=47 cm) is excluded from model curves and RMSE (index nn=2:12, L64) while data curves use all 12 (n=1:12, L63) -- rationale not stated.
